witness.ruling: OW-31: Byzantine primary, SBLGNT secondary; neither is preferred here

numbering: identity: WEB = RP = SBLGNT verse for verse on all 437 verses in 16 chapters (web_greek_offset_map.json identity_throughout true, zones empty). There is no numbering zone.
numbering_face_obligation_on_consumers: every ref here is on the WEB face, which equals the Greek face verse for verse (identity). verse_inventory.json beside it declares the WEB face too. A consumer still asserts the face it expects before verse arithmetic and maps through cor_lib.web_to_greek, which is range-guarded.
method: word-bounded skeleton match. Each verse of each witness is tokenised into greek_lib.skeleton words (NFD, combining marks removed, casefold, final sigma to σ, elision deleted; punctuation and the SBLGNT signs become separators); the token list is asserted equal to skeleton(verse).split(). A pattern is a list of alternative skeleton word sequences, matched by token equality and re-checked with greek_lib.bounded_find. Position classes come from the raw separators: sentence_start (verse-initial after a verse ending in . ; · or the book start, or after . ; · within the verse), verse_initial_mid_sentence, after_comma, after_other_punct, internal. Punctuation is each EDITION's, so position classes are per witness. Counts are of VERSES containing a form, per witness. The substring reading is reported per formula.

web_format.note: 1Cor_web_clean.txt has one '[v] N' line per verse plus paragraph and poetry continuation lines; every WEB quotation is sliced from a single line and asserted byte-exact in the file

citation_sweep_constants.face_basis: Daniel's citation_sweep.py compares its calendar pairs on the MT face: DATELINE_PAIRS, CAL_DATE_PAIRS and CAL_NO_ONSET are MT pairs (lines 303-308), and the onset arm converts a WEB span with web_to_mt before the membership test (lines 389-393). In 1 Corinthians cor_lib.web_to_mt is web_to_greek, identity on all 437 verses, so these pairs are on the WEB face and equal the Greek (RP and SBLGNT) face verse for verse; a consumer still converts through the range-guarded function.
citation_sweep_constants.pairs_taken_from: the RP (primary) verse lists; any SBLGNT-only hit is listed separately
citation_sweep_constants.FRAME_edges_statement: FRAME_PAIRS = frame-formula RP hits before the first APPEAL pair or at/after the first frame-formula hit of the last chapter that has one; FRAME_IN_BODY_PAIRS = the other frame-formula RP hits. An orchestrator amendment of the lane's builder, named for the Fable end review.
citation_sweep_constants.DEVICE_NO_ONSET_statement: empty: no 1 Corinthians ruling restricts onsets at any device. Daniel's CAL_NO_ONSET was also empty and Ezekiel's came from that book's own ruling; neither carries over. These constants record facts only (which verses carry which form), never an onset rule.

how_these_are_used: RULE: these are EVIDENCE, not a verdict. No boundary is set by a count alone; edition punctuation, edition paragraphing and translation formatting never drive one (E-23).
RULE: a refrain CLOSES a unit, so a closing formula (grace benediction, ἀμήν, a doxology) belongs to the unit BEFORE it.
RULE: a seam is assessed from BOTH sides; an onset-only diagnosis is incomplete until the adjacent unit's close is weighed from bytes.
RULE: refs are WEB = Greek (identity); assert the face anyway before comparing.

RULE: quote RP (primary); where RP and SBLGNT disagree on a hit, disclose both and argue from neither alone. A disagreement whose cause is 'position class only' is an edition-punctuation fact, not a textual variant.
RULE: a sentence_start position rests on the edition's punctuation; it is evidence about the edition, not about the author.
HYPOTHESIS to test: a sentence-initial περὶ δέ opens a topic section; weigh each against the close of the section before it, and weigh a mid-clause περὶ δέ separately.
HYPOTHESIS to test: disclosure (οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, γνωρίζω ὑμῖν) and appeal (παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς) formulae open units; test each from both sides.
HYPOTHESIS to test: the vocative ἀδελφοί marks a turn or an appeal, but it is too frequent to set a boundary alone; the skeleton cannot separate vocative from nominative.
HYPOTHESIS to test: citation formulae (γέγραπται, λέγει) and rhetorical οὐκ οἴδατε introduce support inside a unit and are weak boundary signals.

HYPOTHESIS to test: the epistolary frame (prescript, salutation, thanksgiving, greetings, benediction) brackets the body; the thanksgiving verb also stands outside the frame, so the verb alone does not mark it.
HYPOTHESIS to test: question openers (τί οὖν, τί γάρ, μὴ γένοιτο) step an argument within a unit.
